notes.text: Bethlehem — Bethlehem of Judah was called Ephratah, from the fruitfulness of the land where it stood: the word whence it is derived importing fruitfulness. Art thou little - If thou art the least in other respects in this thou art honoured above them all. Ruler - King and sovereign. In Israel - Amidst the Israel of God. Going forth - Whose generation, as he is the Son of God, equal with his father, is eternal.

He — God. Give them up - To the Chaldeans. She - The daughter of Zion, compared here to a woman in travail, shall be delivered out of captivity. His brethren -- the brethren of the Messiah. Those of Judah and Benjamin who were carried captive.

He — The ruler, the Messiah shall stand. This posture speaks the readiness, chearfulness, and stability of Christ, his government, and kingdom. Feed - As a shepherd that diligently guides, preserves, and feeds his sheep. By the strength - By his own almighty strength. Of the name - By commission from the Father in whose name Christ came, preached, wrought miracles, and instituted his gospel church. They - His church made up of converted Jews and Gentiles, shall continue; the gates of hell shall not prevail against them. For - The church is so redeemed, and established, that Christ the Messiah might be glorified, throughout the world.

This man — The Messiah. The peace - Which is promised to the people of God; all their deliverances are not only for his sake, but effected by his power. Shall tread in our palaces - Which Sennacherib did in all the cities of Judah, except Jerusalem. We - Hezekiah, and with him the prophets and people, shall prevail with God to send deliverance. Seven shepherds - A certain number put for an uncertain.
And Mary said — Under a prophetic impulse, several things, which perhaps she herself did not then fully understand.

My spirit hath rejoiced in God my saviour — She seems to turn her thoughts here to Christ himself, who was to be born of her, as the angel had told her, he should be the Son of the Highest, whose name should be Jesus, the saviour. And she rejoiced in hope of salvation through faith in him, which is a blessing common to all true believers, more than in being his mother after the flesh, which was an honour peculiar to her. And certainly she had the same reason to rejoice in God her saviour hat we have: because he had regarded the low estate of his handmaid, in like manner as he regarded our low estate; and vouchsafed to come and save her and us, when we were reduced to the lowest estate of sin and misery.

He hath wrought strength with his arm — That is, he hath shown the exceeding greatness of his power. She speaks prophetically of those things as already done, which God was about to do by the Messiah. He hath scattered the proud - Visible and invisible.
He hath put down the mighty — Both angels and men.
He hath helped his servant Israel — By sending the Messiah.
To his seed — His spiritual seed: all true believers.

glossa.text: *My soul doth magnify the Lord. ((ID.))* First she professes the gifts spiritually granted to her, etc., *as far as* I spend in the keeping of his commandments.

*And hath exulted. ((ID.)) ((ID.))* Because I do not care for earthly things, prosperity does not soften me, adversity does not break me, but the memory of him alone delights me, from whom eternal salvation is hoped for; I rejoice in the Godhead of him by whose conception in time my flesh is made fruitful.

*Because he hath regarded. ((ID.))* Behold how lowly are the things she feels concerning herself, etc., *as far as* and out of the small and the weak he makes them great and strong.

*Because he hath done great things to me.* Because in me he took flesh, and cleansed me from sins, and conferred upon me the gifts of the Holy Ghost.

 *And mercy. ((BEDA.))* From the special gifts she turns herself to the general judgments of God, etc., *as far as* he adds what the despisers deserve.

*He hath filled the hungry with good things. ((ID.))* They who desire eternal things with all zeal; shall be filled, when Christ shall have appeared in glory. But they who rejoice in earthly things are sent away at the last empty of all blessedness. In the present life also we see the humble filled with divine grace, and the proud deprived of the light of truth.

*As he spoke to our fathers.* Making mention of the fathers to whom this salvation was revealed, she names Abraham expressly, to whom the incarnation itself was first made manifest. *And to his seed for ever.* Not so much to those born of the flesh as to those who have followed the footsteps of faith, to whom the coming of the Saviour was promised for ever, because the promise of the inheritance itself shall be closed by no end. For both unto the end of the world believers shall not be lacking, and the glory of blessedness shall be everlasting.

notes.text: When he cometh into the world — In the fortieth Psalm the Messiah's coming into the world is represented. It is said, into the world, not into the tabernacle, chap. ix, 1; because all the world is interested in his sacrifice. A body hast thou prepared for me - That I may offer up myself. Psalm xl, 6, &c.
In the volume of the book — In this very psalm it is written of me. Accordingly I come to do thy will - By the sacrifice of myself.
Above when he said, Sacrifice thou hast not chosen — That is, when the Psalmist pronounced those words in his name.

Then said he — in that very instant he subjoined. Lo, I come to do Thy will - To offer a more acceptable sacrifice; and by this very act he taketh away the legal, that he may establish the evangelical, dispensation.
By which will — Of God, done and suffered by Christ. We are sanctified - Cleansed from guilt, and consecrated to God.

glossa.text: *Thou wouldst not.* From the time of the passion, in which is the consummation of all victims, those things began to displease. He never destroyed them before, but was subject to them, when he was presented in the temple with victims. *But a body thou hast fitted to me.* The signs are taken away, because the truth has been shown forth, then was the time that those should be taken away, and the truth should come. Nor was the Lord ever delighted in those odours, save in the faith and the desire of him that offered. Yet he commanded these things to be offered to himself, rather than that they should be offered to idols; and he imposed them for servitude, not for justification, and that they might be a figure of what was to come.

*They have not pleased.* In those figures the truth was foretold. They celebrate figures, many knowing the thing of the figure, but more not knowing it, which figures must cease when the thing has been shown forth.

*Then.* When I saw that all those things displeased, and that a body fit for this was given to me. *I said: Behold I come,* to offer myself, that I may do and fulfil thy will, because thou art my God. Therefore I come to fulfil thy thy will, because so it is written, and prefigured concerning me in the counsel of the Godhead, which is my head, I who am the book of the human race according as I am man, in which book let men read all things necessary for them, and therefore there is no need of the law.

*Saying above.* As if he should say: This authority notes not only that the old victims did not make men perfect, but that the victim of Christ alone did; but also the taking away of the Old Testament, and the establishing of the New, if the words be diligently noted; because, saying above, *thou wouldst not have those things,* he adds: *Then I said.* For behold, he takes away the first sacrifice and with it the Old Testament, and appoints as stable the new sacrifice and with it the New Testament.
*Sanctified,* etc. The purgation of sins having been made, we are reconciled to God.

notes.text: A city of Judah — Probably Hebron, which was situated in the hill country of Judea, and belonged to the house of Aaron.

When Elisabeth heard the salutation of Mary — The discourse with which she saluted her, giving an account of what the angel had said, the joy of her soul so affected her body, that the very child in her womb was moved in an uncommon manner, as if it leaped for joy.
Happy is she that believed — Probably she had in her mind the unbelief of Zacharias.
And Mary said — Under a prophetic impulse, several things, which perhaps she herself did not then fully understand.

My spirit hath rejoiced in God my saviour — She seems to turn her thoughts here to Christ himself, who was to be born of her, as the angel had told her, he should be the Son of the Highest, whose name should be Jesus, the saviour. And she rejoiced in hope of salvation through faith in him, which is a blessing common to all true believers, more than in being his mother after the flesh, which was an honour peculiar to her. And certainly she had the same reason to rejoice in God her saviour hat we have: because he had regarded the low estate of his handmaid, in like manner as he regarded our low estate; and vouchsafed to come and save her and us, when we were reduced to the lowest estate of sin and misery.

He hath wrought strength with his arm — That is, he hath shown the exceeding greatness of his power. She speaks prophetically of those things as already done, which God was about to do by the Messiah. He hath scattered the proud - Visible and invisible.
He hath put down the mighty — Both angels and men.
He hath helped his servant Israel — By sending the Messiah.
To his seed — His spiritual seed: all true believers.

glossa.text: *And Mary rising up in those days, went into the hill country with haste into a city of Juda. ((AMBR.))* Not incredulous of the oracle, etc., *as far as* when it is added: *And it came to pass, that when she heard.*

*And she entered into the house of Zachary.* From this let holy women learn what attentiveness they ought to show to kinswomen with child.

*And saluted Elizabeth. ((BEDA.))* She salutes first, because it is fitting that the chaster she is, the humbler she should be.

*He exulted,* etc. Because he could not with the tongue, he salutes with an exulting spirit, and begins the office of his forerunning. Behold, there appears what the angel had said: *He shall be filled with the Holy Ghost even from his mother's womb.*

*Blessed art thou. ((BEDA, AMBR.))* The words of the Gospel agree with the words of the psalm in which it is promised to David: *Of the fruit of thy womb I will set upon thy throne ((Psal. CXXXI))*. And Mary is blessed by Elizabeth with the same voice as by Gabriel, so that she may be shown venerable both to angels and to men, and to be preferred before our women.
*The mother of the Lord.* I perceive the miracle, I acknowledge the mystery: the mother of the Lord, teeming with the Word, full of God.

*As was made.* In the very moment in which the voice enters the ears of the body, a spiritual power enters the heart of the hearer, and kindles not only the mother but also the offspring with love of her who comes.

*He exulted. ((BEDA.))* By the revealing of the Spirit with whom she was filled, etc., *as far as* the virgin believed where the priest denied.
*My soul doth magnify the Lord. ((ID.))* First she professes the gifts spiritually granted to her, etc., *as far as* I spend in the keeping of his commandments.

*And hath exulted. ((ID.)) ((ID.))* Because I do not care for earthly things, prosperity does not soften me, adversity does not break me, but the memory of him alone delights me, from whom eternal salvation is hoped for; I rejoice in the Godhead of him by whose conception in time my flesh is made fruitful.

*Because he hath regarded. ((ID.))* Behold how lowly are the things she feels concerning herself, etc., *as far as* and out of the small and the weak he makes them great and strong.

*Because he hath done great things to me.* Because in me he took flesh, and cleansed me from sins, and conferred upon me the gifts of the Holy Ghost.

 *And mercy. ((BEDA.))* From the special gifts she turns herself to the general judgments of God, etc., *as far as* he adds what the despisers deserve.

*As he spoke to our fathers.* Making mention of the fathers to whom this salvation was revealed, she names Abraham expressly, to whom the incarnation itself was first made manifest. *And to his seed for ever.* Not so much to those born of the flesh as to those who have followed the footsteps of faith, to whom the coming of the Saviour was promised for ever, because the promise of the inheritance itself shall be closed by no end. echoes.attribution: Catena, CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wilson Pruitt / Wroot Press)

echoes.text: Hannah prayed, and said: “My heart exults in Yahweh! My horn is exalted in Yahweh. My mouth is enlarged over my enemies, because I rejoice in your salvation.
echoes.note: The Magnificat's opening, 'My soul magnifies the Lord, my spirit has rejoiced in God my Savior,' is modeled directly on Hannah's Song: 'My heart exults in the Lord... I rejoice in your salvation' (1 Samuel 2:1). Hannah's hymn is the structural template for the whole canticle; high volume and strong recurrence.

echoes.text: She vowed a vow, and said, “Yahweh of Armies, if you will indeed look on the affliction of your handmaid, and remember me, and not forget your handmaid, but will give to your handmaid a boy, then I will give him to Yahweh all the days of his life, and no razor shall come on his head.”
echoes.note: 'He has looked at the humble state (tapeinosin) of his handmaid' quotes Hannah's prayer that God would 'look on the affliction (tapeinosin) of your handmaid' (1 Samuel 1:11 LXX). The shared rare-noun + handmaid combination is high-volume and ties the canticle's singer to Hannah.

echoes.text: Leah said, “Happy am I, for the daughters will call me happy.” She named him Asher.
echoes.note: 'From now on, all generations will call me blessed' takes up Leah's 'the women will call me blessed' (Genesis 30:13 LXX), spoken at the birth of a son. The call-me-blessed formula is distinctive matriarchal speech, here universalized to all generations.

echoes.text: He has sent redemption to his people. He has ordained his covenant forever. His name is holy and awesome!
echoes.note: 'Holy is his name' quotes Psalm 111:9, 'holy and awesome is his name' (cf. Psalm 99:3). The fixed liturgical predication of the divine name gives high volume; Psalm 111 also feeds the Benedictus (1:68), showing recurrence.

echoes.text: But Yahweh’s loving kindness is from everlasting to everlasting with those who fear him, his righteousness to children’s children;
echoes.note: 'His mercy is for generations of generations on those who fear him' quotes Psalm 103:17, 'the steadfast love of the Lord is from everlasting to everlasting on those who fear him.' The mercy + on-those-who-fear-him + perpetual-generations combination is high-volume and distinctive.

echoes.text: yet I will rejoice in Yahweh. I will be joyful in the God of my salvation!
echoes.note: 'My spirit has rejoiced in God my Savior' closely matches 'I will rejoice in the Lord; I will take joy in the God of my salvation' (Habakkuk 3:18 LXX). The rejoice-in-God-my-savior formula is distinctive and reinforces the exultant-prophetic-hymn register.

echoes.text: My soul shall be joyful in Yahweh. It shall rejoice in his salvation.
echoes.note: 'My soul shall rejoice in the Lord, exulting in his salvation' (Psalm 35:9) supplies the soul-rejoices-in-salvation diction underlying 1:47. A coherent psalmic echo within the cluster of rejoicing-in-God's-deliverance texts.

echoes.text: I will greatly rejoice in Yahweh, my soul shall be joyful in my God; for he has clothed me with the garments of salvation, he has covered me with the robe of righteousness, as a bridegroom decks himself with a garland, and as a bride adorns herself with her jewels.
echoes.note: 'My soul shall exult in my God' (Isaiah 61:10) within the Spirit-anointed-good-news passage contributes to the rejoicing diction of the canticle's opening. Thematic coherence with eschatological salvation supports the echo.

echoes.text: Leah conceived, and bore a son, and she named him Reuben. For she said, “Because Yahweh has looked at my affliction. For now my husband will love me.”
echoes.note: 'He has looked at the humble state' also echoes Leah's 'the Lord has looked upon my affliction' at Reuben's birth (Genesis 29:32 LXX). The look-on-affliction-of-the-lowly motif coheres with the matriarchal reversal theme; a supporting echo to the Hannah primary.

echoes.text: Then our mouth was filled with laughter, and our tongue with singing. Then they said among the nations, “Yahweh has done great things for them.” Yahweh has done great things for us, and we are glad.
echoes.note: 'He who is mighty has done great things for me' echoes 'The Lord has done great things for us; we are glad' (Psalm 126:2-3). The great-things-the-Lord-has-done formula is a coherent psalmic source for the canticle's praise.

echoes.text: He is your praise, and he is your God, who has done for you these great and awesome things, which your eyes have seen.
echoes.note: 'He... has done great things for me' also recalls 'He is your praise; he is your God, who has done for you these great and awesome things' (Deuteronomy 10:21). A further great-deeds source coherent with the doxological tone.

echoes.text: and showing loving kindness to thousands of those who love me and keep my commandments.
echoes.note: 'His mercy is for generations... on those who fear him' echoes the Decalogue's promise of steadfast love 'to thousands of those who love me and keep my commandments' (Exodus 20:6; Deuteronomy 5:10). The covenant mercy-to-generations formula coheres with Psalm 103.

echoes.text: You have broken Rahab in pieces, like one of the slain. You have scattered your enemies with your mighty arm.
echoes.note: 'He has shown strength with his arm. He has scattered the proud' echoes Psalm 89:10, 'you scattered your enemies with your mighty arm.' The arm + scatter combination is distinctive, and Psalm 89 (Davidic covenant) coheres with the chapter's throne themes; high volume.

echoes.text: “Talk no more so exceeding proudly. Don’t let arrogance come out of your mouth, For Yahweh is a God of knowledge. By him actions are weighed. “The bows of the mighty men are broken. Those who stumbled are armed with strength.
echoes.note: 'He has scattered the proud in the imagination of their hearts' draws on Hannah's warning, 'Talk no more so very proudly... the bows of the mighty are broken' (1 Samuel 2:3-4). The humbling-of-the-arrogant motif is structurally central to Hannah's Song, the canticle's master text.

echoes.text: Yahweh makes poor, and makes rich. He brings low, he also lifts up. He raises up the poor out of the dust. He lifts up the needy from the dunghill, To make them sit with princes, and inherit the throne of glory. For the pillars of the earth are Yahweh’s. He has set the world on them.
echoes.note: 'He has put down princes from their thrones, and has exalted the lowly' directly reworks Hannah: 'The Lord makes poor and makes rich; he brings low and he exalts. He raises up the poor from the dust... to make them sit with princes' (1 Samuel 2:7-8). High volume; the great-reversal heart of the Magnificat.

echoes.text: Those who were full have hired themselves out for bread. Those who were hungry are satisfied. Yes, the barren has borne seven. She who has many children languishes.
echoes.note: 'He has filled the hungry with good things. He has sent the rich away empty' reworks Hannah's 'those who were full have hired themselves out for bread, but the hungry have ceased to hunger' (1 Samuel 2:5). The hungry-filled / sated-emptied antithesis is high-volume and distinctive.

echoes.text: For he satisfies the longing soul. He fills the hungry soul with good.
echoes.note: 'He has filled the hungry with good things' quotes Psalm 107:9, 'he satisfies the longing soul, and the hungry soul he fills with good things.' Near-verbatim; a strong psalmic doublet to the Hannah hunger-reversal.

echoes.text: He raises up the poor out of the dust. Lifts up the needy from the ash heap; that he may set him with princes, even with the princes of his people.
echoes.note: 'Has exalted the lowly' reflects Psalm 113:7-8, 'He raises the poor from the dust... to make them sit with princes.' Psalm 113 (a Hallel psalm) shares both the lifting-the-lowly motif and its own debt to Hannah; high volume within the reversal cluster.

echoes.text: “But you, Israel, my servant, Jacob whom I have chosen, the seed of Abraham my friend, You whom I have taken hold of from the ends of the earth, and called from its corners, and said to you, ‘You are my servant, I have chosen you and not cast you away;’
echoes.note: 'He has given help to Israel, his servant' draws on Isaiah 41:8-9, 'But you, Israel, my servant... whom I have taken... I have chosen you and not cast you off.' The Israel-my-servant designation plus God's helping/upholding (Isaiah 41:10) gives high volume for the canticle's turn to corporate Israel.

echoes.text: He has remembered his loving kindness and his faithfulness toward the house of Israel. All the ends of the earth have seen the salvation of our God.
echoes.note: 'That he might remember mercy' quotes Psalm 98:3, 'He has remembered his steadfast love and faithfulness to the house of Israel.' The remembered-mercy-to-Israel formula is distinctive and rounds off the canticle's covenant-faithfulness theme.

echoes.text: You will give truth to Jacob, and mercy to Abraham, as you have sworn to our fathers from the days of old.
echoes.note: 'As he spoke to our fathers, to Abraham and his seed forever' echoes Micah 7:20, 'You will show faithfulness to Jacob and steadfast love to Abraham, as you have sworn to our fathers from the days of old.' The mercy-to-Abraham-as-sworn-to-the-fathers structure is high-volume and concludes both hymns (cf. 1:73).

echoes.text: I will establish my covenant between me and you and your seed after you throughout their generations for an everlasting covenant, to be a God to you and to your seed after you.
echoes.note: 'To Abraham and his seed forever' takes up the Abrahamic covenant, 'to be God to you and to your offspring after you... an everlasting covenant' (Genesis 17:7; cf. 13:15). The to-Abraham-and-his-seed-forever formula is distinctive covenant language; high volume.

echoes.text: He leads priests away stripped, and overthrows the mighty.
echoes.note: 'He has put down princes from their thrones' echoes Job 12:19, 'he leads priests away stripped and overthrows the mighty.' Job 12's catalogue of God's reversal of the powerful (12:14-25) coheres with the Magnificat's social inversion; a focused supporting allusion.

echoes.text: The Lord cast down the thrones of rulers, And set the meek in their stead.
echoes.note: 'He has put down princes from their thrones' closely matches Sirach 10:14, 'The Lord has cast down the thrones of rulers, and has seated the lowly in their place.' A deuterocanonical near-parallel with the throne-down / lowly-up structure; strong coherence, moderate independent volume.

echoes.text: thus says the Lord Yahweh: Remove the turban, and take off the crown; this will not be as it was; exalt that which is low, and abase that which is high.
echoes.note: 'Put down princes from their thrones... exalted the lowly' echoes Ezekiel 21:26, 'exalt that which is low, and abase that which is high.' The abase-the-high / exalt-the-low formula coheres with the inversion theme as a prophetic supporting echo.

echoes.text: that I will bless you greatly, and I will multiply your seed greatly like the stars of the heavens, and like the sand which is on the seashore. Your seed will possess the gate of his enemies.
echoes.note: 'And his seed forever' also recalls the oath at the Aqedah, 'I will surely multiply your offspring' (Genesis 22:17), the same sworn promise the Benedictus names explicitly at 1:73. A coherent supporting echo binding Magnificat and Benedictus.

echoes.text: Yahweh’s ark remained in the house of Obed-Edom the Gittite three months: and Yahweh blessed Obed-Edom, and all his house.
echoes.note: 'Mary stayed with her about three months' parallels the ark of God remaining 'in the house of Obed-edom... three months' (2 Samuel 6:11). Combined with the ark allusions of 1:43-44, the three-month notice supports the Mary-as-ark typology; figural and contested.

harmony.note: Mary's song — "he has put down princes from their thrones, and has exalted the lowly."

echoes.text: The children struggled together within her. She said, “If it be so, why do I live?” She went to inquire of Yahweh.
echoes.note: 'The baby leaped in her womb' recalls the children who 'struggled (leaped) together within' Rebekah (Genesis 25:22 LXX), the one OT scene of pre-natal movement bearing prophetic significance about the elder/younger. The distinctive womb-movement motif gives high volume.

echoes.text: You shall be blessed in the fruit of your body, the fruit of your ground, the fruit of your animals, the increase of your livestock, and the young of your flock.
echoes.note: 'Blessed is the fruit of your womb' quotes the covenant blessing of Deuteronomy 28:4, 'Blessed shall be the fruit of your womb.' The exact fruit-of-the-womb-blessing formula gives high volume and casts Mary's child as the supreme covenant blessing.

echoes.text: “Jael shall be blessed above women, the wife of Heber the Kenite; blessed shall she be above women in the tent.
echoes.note: 'Blessed are you among women' repeats the Jael blessing of Judges 5:24, now on Elizabeth's lips. Recurrence (cf. 1:28) confirms this as a deliberate, sustained scriptural beatitude pattern.

echoes.text: Ozias said to her, “Blessed are you, daughter, in the sight of the Most High God, above all the women upon the earth; and blessed is the Lord God, who created the heavens and the earth, who directed you to cut off the head of the prince of our enemies.
echoes.note: Elizabeth's acclamation matches Uzziah's blessing of Judith, 'Blessed are you above all women on earth' (Judith 13:18), the nearest verbal parallel for the woman-through-whom-God-delivers beatitude. A strong deuterocanonical recurrence.

echoes.text: David was afraid of Yahweh that day; and he said, “How shall Yahweh’s ark come to me?”
echoes.note: 'Why am I so favored, that the mother of my Lord should come to me?' echoes David's awe before the ark: 'How can the ark of the Lord come to me?' (2 Samuel 6:9). With Mary's three-month stay (1:56) paralleling the ark's three months (2 Samuel 6:11), Luke figurally presents Mary as the ark of the new covenant; the reading is widely held but disputed.

echoes.text: David danced before Yahweh with all his might; and David was clothed in a linen ephod. So David and all the house of Israel brought up Yahweh’s ark with shouting, and with the sound of the trumpet. It was so, as Yahweh’s ark came into the city of David, that Michal the daughter of Saul looked out at the window, and saw king David leaping and dancing before Yahweh; and she despised him in her heart.
echoes.note: 'The baby leaped in my womb for joy' echoes David's leaping and dancing for joy before the ark (2 Samuel 6:14-16). The cultic joy before the bearer of the Lord's presence supports the Mary-as-ark typology of the pericope; the link is figural and contested.

registers.label: Spare
lines: From little Bethlehem comes the one who will shepherd us.
My soul magnifies the Lord.
The child leaps in the womb at the sound of grace.
My soul magnifies the Lord.
God has lifted up the lowly and filled the hungry with good things.
Come, let us worship. Amen.

registers.label: Immersive
lines: Two women meet at a doorway, and a child leaps for joy before he can speak.
My soul magnifies the Lord.
The young one is carrying God; the old promise is coming true between them.
My soul magnifies the Lord.
God has scattered the proud and lifted the lowly, filled the hungry, kept every word.
My soul magnifies the Lord.
So from the smallest places, from the overlooked and the unlikely, mercy is being born.
My soul magnifies the Lord, and my spirit rejoices!

registers.label: Hybrid
lines: From little Bethlehem, a shepherd; in a young woman, God.
My soul magnifies the Lord.
The child leaps for joy at grace arriving.
My soul magnifies the Lord.
The lowly lifted, the hungry filled.
My soul magnifies the Lord. Amen.
